items.title: Graphing a Transformed Reciprocal Function

sections.normalized_html:
To plot [MATH: y = -\dfrac{2}{x-1}-1,] we apply the following steps:

  • Take the curve [MATH: y=-\dfrac{1}{x}.]

  • Translate it by one unit to the right to get the graph of [MATH: y=-\dfrac{1}{x-1}.]

    Notice that the vertical asymptote is now [MATH: x=1.]

  • Then, stretch the result by a scale factor of [MATH: 2] parallel to the [MATH: y]-axis to get the graph of [MATH: y=-\dfrac{2}{x-1}.]

  • Finally, translate it by [MATH: 1] unit down to get the graph of [MATH: y=-\dfrac{2}{x-1}-1.]

    Notice that the horizontal asymptote is now [MATH: y=-1.]

items.title: Solving for Some Unknowns Given the Graph of a Transformed Reciprocal Function

sections.normalized_html: The diagram above shows the graph of [MATH: y = \dfrac{a}{x-b}+k.] What is the value of [MATH: a+b+k?]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/daf6141f9c6d989c76e8b22ea3252d2b]

The diagram above shows the graph of [MATH: y = \dfrac{a}{x-b}+k.] What is the value of [MATH: a+b+k?]

sections.normalized_html:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is [MATH: y=-1,] while the vertical asymptote is [MATH: x=2.] This means that [MATH: k=-1] and [MATH: b=2,] and we can re-write our function as

[MATH: y = \dfrac{a}{x-2}+(-1) = \dfrac{a}{x-2}-1.]

Also, we are given that the point [MATH: (3,2)] lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

[MATH: y|= (a)/(x − 2) − 1; 2|= (a)/(3 − 2) − 1; 3|= (a)/(1); a|= 3.]

Finally, [MATH: a+b+k = 3+2+(-1) = 4.]

Item 13 — Example: Solving for Some Unknowns Given the Graph of a Transformed Reciprocal Function

Example Prompt:
[IMG: /graphics/daf6141f9c6d989c76e8b22ea3252d2b]

The diagram above shows the graph of [MATH: y = \dfrac{a}{x-b}+k.] What is the value of [MATH: a+b+k?]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is [MATH: y=-1,] while the vertical asymptote is [MATH: x=2.] This means that [MATH: k=-1] and [MATH: b=2,] and we can re-write our function as

[MATH: y = \dfrac{a}{x-2}+(-1) = \dfrac{a}{x-2}-1.]

Also, we are given that the point [MATH: (3,2)] lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

[MATH: y|= (a)/(x − 2) − 1; 2|= (a)/(3 − 2) − 1; 3|= (a)/(1); a|= 3.]

Finally, [MATH: a+b+k = 3+2+(-1) = 4.]
